## Story-level uncertainties

- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: she is called Asiya, and later works describe her faith and her end.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Her words about the child  (`#her-words-about-the-child`)

Cited ayat: 28:9

> **28:9** وَقَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِّى وَلَكَ لَا تَقْتُلُوهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (28:9): The wife of Fir'awn said that he would be a source of comfort to her and to Fir'awn.

**c2** (28:9): She said not to kill him, since perhaps he would benefit them or they might adopt him as a son.

**c3** (28:9): The ayah adds that they did not perceive.

### One-minute summary

The wife of Fir'awn said that he would be a source of comfort to her and to Fir'awn [c1]. She said not to kill him, since perhaps he would benefit them or they might adopt him as a son [c2].

### Complete story

The wife of Fir'awn said that he would be a source of comfort to her and to Fir'awn [c1]. She said not to kill him, since perhaps he would benefit them or they might adopt him as a son [c2]. The ayah adds that they did not perceive [c3].

### Deep study

The ayah does not name the one she speaks of and refers to him only as him [c1]. The words they did not perceive are given after her speech and do not say who is meant [c3].

### Kids mode

The wife of Fir'awn said that he would be a comfort to her and to Fir'awn [c1]. She said not to kill him [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that her words hope that he might benefit them or be adopted as a son [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: her name, or whether she believed at the time of these words.
- Not established in this ayah: who she is speaking about; the pronoun refers to the child mentioned in the previous ayah.
- Not established: who they are in the words they did not perceive, or what they did not perceive.

## 2. Her prayer  (`#her-prayer`)

Cited ayat: 66:11

> **66:11** وَضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱمْرَأَتَ فِرْعَوْنَ إِذْ قَالَتْ رَبِّ ٱبْنِ لِى عِندَكَ بَيْتًا فِى ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَنَجِّنِى مِن فِرْعَوْنَ وَعَمَلِهِۦ وَنَجِّنِى مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (66:11): God presented the wife of Fir'awn as an example for those who believe, when she said, my Lord, build me a house with You in the Garden, save me from Fir'awn and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people.

### One-minute summary

God presented the wife of Fir'awn as an example for those who believe [c1]. She asked her Lord to build her a house with Him in the Garden and to save her from Fir'awn and his deeds [c1].

### Complete story

God presented the wife of Fir'awn as an example for those who believe, when she said, my Lord, build me a house with You in the Garden, save me from Fir'awn and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people [c1].

### Deep study

The ayah says that God set her forth as an example for those who believe, and it gives her prayer [c1]. It does not say when she prayed [c1].

### Kids mode

The wife of Fir'awn asked her Lord to build her a house with Him in the Garden [c1]. She also asked Him to save her from Fir'awn and his deeds [c1].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah presents her prayer as an example for those who believe [c1].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: when she prayed, or what became of her.
- Not established: whether she is the same woman as the one who spoke about the child, beyond the title the wife of Fir'awn.
